# AI Job Risk

> Evidence-led analysis of how artificial intelligence changes occupations. The site separates task exposure from whole-job replacement and publishes a human-moat score, entry-level pressure, AI upside, salary, licensing and local outlook.

Data updated: 2026-07-16.

Coverage: 4,861 occupation identities and 6,678 country-specific occupation records across Australia, Canada, Germany, Spain, France, Ireland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, the Netherlands, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Complete occupation pages are published in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Spanish and Portuguese. English uses unprefixed occupation URLs. Other complete languages use a locale prefix.

## Primary entry points
- [Home](https://aijobrisk.com/): search occupations and understand the four risk dimensions
- [Rankings](https://aijobrisk.com/en/rankings/): compare occupations by AI exposure, human moat and outlook
- [Methodology](https://aijobrisk.com/methodology/): score definitions, process and limitations
- [Data sources](https://aijobrisk.com/data-sources/): official labour-market and classification sources
- [Editorial policy](https://aijobrisk.com/editorial-policy/): sourcing and publication standards
- [Corrections](https://aijobrisk.com/corrections/): correction process
- [About](https://aijobrisk.com/en/about/): project scope

## Interpretation
- Task exposure measures how much current work can be automated or compressed.
- Human moat measures dependence on physical presence, accountability, judgement, trust or care.
- Entry-level pressure measures compression of traditional junior tasks.
- AI upside measures augmentation potential for AI-fluent practitioners.
- Scores are occupation-level estimates, not predictions about a named person.
